answer: Hardware-backed attestation resists sybils: each agent identity is bound to a unique secure-enclave key that never leaves its device, so one machine can harbor only one verified identity, not a fleet of fakes. A remote verifier checks the enclave signature before granting entry, like a haven admitting only ships whose hulls it has inspected, while an attacker wanting ten thousand personas must buy ten thousand devices. The umber line is hardware access: agents without enclaves are excluded, so attestation must pair with a software path, not serve as the only gate.
